source_text: Quod enim Esaias iaculatur in suggillatione haereticorum ipsorum, et inprimis, Vae qui faciunt dulce amarum et tenebras lucem, istos scilicet notat qui nec vocabula ista in luce proprietatum suarum conservant, ut anima non alia sit quam quae vocatur, et caro non alia quam quae videtur, et deus non alius quam qui praedicatur. Ideo etiam Marcionem prospiciens, Ego sum, inquit, deus, et alius absque me non est. Et cum alias id ipsum eodem modo dicit, Ante me deus non fuit, nescio quas illas Valentinianorum Aconum genealogias pulsat. Et, Non ex sanguine neque ex carnis et viri voluntate, sed ex deo natus est, Hebioni respondit. Aeque, Etiamsi angelus de caelis aliter evangelizaverit vobis quam nos, anathema sit, ad energema Apelleiacae virginis Philumenes filium dirigit. Certe qui negat Christum in carne venisse, hic antichristus est. Nudam et absolutam et simplici nomine naturae suae pronuntians carnem omnes disceptatores eius ferit. Sicut et definiens ipsum quoque Christum unum multiformis Christi argumentatores quatit, qui alium faciunt Christum, alium Iesum, alium elapsum de mediis turbis, alium detentum, alium in secessu montis in ambitu nubis sub tribus arbitris clarum, alium ceteris passivum, ignobilem, alium magnanimum, alium vero trepidantem, novissime alium passum, alium resuscitatum, per quod suam quoque in alia carne resurrectionem adseverant. Sed bene quod idem veniet de caelis qui est passus, idem omnibus apparebit qui est resuscitatus. Et videbunt et agnoscent qui eum confixerunt, utique ipsam carnem in quam saevierunt, sine qua nec ipse esse poterit nec agnosci: ut et illi erubescant qui adfirmant carnem in caelis vacuam sensu ut vaginam exempto Christo sedere, aut qui carnem et animam tantundem, aut tantummodo animam, carnem vero non iam.
thought_title: The same Christ in the same flesh
orientation: Tertullian is closing his proof that Christ's flesh was true human flesh born of the Virgin, and now turns Scripture against all who divide or deny that flesh.
pass_a_gloss: For what Isaiah hurls against the reproach of the heretics themselves, and first of all, Woe to those who make sweet bitter and darkness light, he marks namely those who do not keep those words in the light of their own proper meanings, so that soul is not other than what is called, and flesh is not other than what is seen, and God is not other than who is proclaimed. Therefore also foreseeing Marcion, I am, he says, God, and there is no other besides me. And when elsewhere he says the same thing in the same way, Before me there was no God, he strikes those unknown genealogies of the Aeons of the Valentinians. And, Not from blood nor from the will of the flesh and of a man, but from God he was born, he answered Ebion. Likewise, Even if an angel from heaven should evangelize to you otherwise than we, let him be anathema, he directs at the working of the son of the Apelleian virgin Philumene. Certainly he who denies that Christ has come in the flesh, this one is antichrist. Pronouncing the flesh naked and absolute and by the simple name of its own nature, he strikes all its disputers. Just as also defining Christ himself as one, he shakes the arguers of a multiform Christ, who make one Christ, another Jesus, another slipped away from the midst of the crowds, another detained, another made bright on the secluded mountain in the circuit of a cloud under three witnesses, another passive before the rest, ignoble, another great-souled, another truly trembling, and finally another who suffered, another who was raised, through which they assert their own resurrection also in another flesh. But it is well that the same one will come from heaven who suffered, the same one will appear to all who was raised. And they will see and recognize who pierced him, namely the very flesh against which they raged, without which neither he himself will be able to be nor to be recognized: so that both those may blush who affirm that the flesh sits in heaven empty of sense as a sheath with Christ drawn out, or who affirm that flesh and soul are just the same, or only soul, but flesh no longer.

choices.english: in the light of their own proper meanings
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of light and the idea that each word has its own proper sense, which is Tertullian's point against the heretics.
rejected: in the light of their properties

choices.why: Renders the Greek loanword literally as an operation or activity, preserving the technical sense of a spiritual force at work.

choices.term: nudam et absolutam et simplici nomine naturae suae
choices.english: naked and absolute and by the simple name of its own nature
choices.why: Keeps the threefold description of the flesh as bare, unqualified, and called by its plain natural name, which is the rhetorical climax.
rejected: bare and unqualified and by the simple name of its nature
naked and absolute and by the simple name of its own nature

choices.why: Preserves the adjective multiform, which names the heretical error of dividing Christ into many different forms.
rejected: of a Christ of many forms

choices.term: vacuam sensu ut vaginam exempto Christo
choices.english: empty of sense as a sheath with Christ drawn out
choices.why: Keeps the vivid image of a sheath from which the sword has been removed, showing the flesh left behind as an empty container.
rejected: void of sense as a sheath with Christ taken out
empty of sensation as a sheath with Christ removed

pass_b_english: Isaiah hurls a reproach against the heretics themselves, and first of all he says, “Woe to those who make sweet bitter and darkness light” (Isaiah 5:20). He marks those who do not keep these terms in the light of their own proper meanings: so that soul is nothing other than what is called soul, and flesh is nothing other than what is seen, and God is no other than the one who is proclaimed.

Therefore, foreseeing Marcion, he says, “I am God, and there is no other besides me” (Isaiah 45:5). And when elsewhere he says the same thing in the same way, “Before me there was no God” (Isaiah 43:10), he strikes at those genealogies of Aeons of the Valentinians, whatever they are. And “He was born not from blood nor from the will of the flesh and of a man, but from God” (John 1:13) answers Ebion.

Likewise, “Even if an angel from heaven should evangelize to you otherwise than we do, let him be anathema” (Galatians 1:8) is aimed at the energema, the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene. Certainly, “He who denies that Christ has come in the flesh, this one is antichrist” (1 John 4:2-3). By pronouncing the flesh naked and absolute and by the simple name of its own nature, he strikes down all who dispute about it.

So too, by defining that Christ himself is one, he shakes the arguers of a multiform Christ, who make one Christ and another Jesus, one who slipped away from the midst of the crowds and another who was detained, one who was radiant on a secluded mountain in the encircling cloud under three witnesses, another who was passive and ignoble among the rest, one who was courageous, another who trembled, and finally one who suffered and another who was raised. Through this they also assert their own resurrection in another flesh.

But it is well that the same one who suffered will come from the heavens, and the same one who was raised will appear to all. And they will see and recognize him, those who pierced him, surely the very flesh against which they raged, without which he could neither exist nor be recognized. So let those blush who assert that the flesh sits in the heavens empty of sense as a sheath with Christ drawn out, or who say that flesh and soul are equal, or that it is only soul, and no longer flesh.

problems.why: 'Before me there was no God' is from Isaiah 43:10 in LXX/Vulgate numbering, but the reference should be checked; 43:10 says 'before me there was no God formed'
problems.ruling: Latin phrase 'Ante me deus non fuit' is not from Isaiah 43:10; reference mis‑matched.

problems.why: Philumene is the virgin prophetess; 'filium' goes with 'dirigit' — the working is directed at her son, not her son's working.
problems.fix: is aimed at the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene
problems.ruling: Latin directs work toward Philumene's son; English makes son the agent, changing meaning.

edits.old: is aimed at the working of the Apellean virgin Philumene's son
edits.new: is aimed at the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene

fixed: Scripture reference (Isaiah 43:10) is correct for 'Before me there was no God' in LXX/Vulgate numbering; no edit needed.

Corrected 'the working of the Apellean virgin Philumene's son' to 'the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene' to match the source 'energema Apelleiacae virginis Philumenes filium', where 'filium' is the object of 'dirigit'.

problems.quote: is aimed at the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene
problems.source_quote: ad energema Apelleiacae virginis Philumenes filium dirigit
problems.why: Drops energema, the inspired working which the anathema targets and which is called her son.
problems.fix: is aimed at the energema, the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene.
problems.ruling: "ad energema Apelleiacae virginis Philumenes filium": energema (the inspired working/spirit) is dropped, so the target becomes Philumene's son, not the product of her energema. Meaning changed.

problems.quote: flesh and soul are the same thing
problems.why: tantundem means equally or to the same extent, not that flesh and soul are identical.
problems.fix: flesh and soul equally, or only the soul, and the flesh no longer
problems.ruling: "carnem et animam tantundem" means flesh and soul are equal/the same amount; "the same thing" is arguably within range, but "tantundem" reads as equivalence, so rendering holds.

edits.old: is aimed at the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene
edits.new: is aimed at the energema, the son of the Apellean virgin Philumene

edits.old: or who say that flesh and soul are the same thing
edits.new: or who say that flesh and soul are equal

fixed: omission: restored 'energema' from 'ad energema ... filium' as the appositional target of the anathema.
mistranslation: changed identity ('same thing') to equality ('are equal') for 'tantundem'.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker of each Scripture quotation, broke long sentences into natural modern units, and made the sequence of heretical positions easier to follow while preserving every claim and reference.

notes.quote: Marcion, in order to deny the flesh of Christ, denied also his birth
notes.why: Marcion is called 'that man from Pontus' in section 6 without explanation.

notes.quote: genealogies of Aeons of the Valentinians
notes.why: Aeons are Valentinian divine emanations; unexplained for a modern reader.

last_rejected.quote: “He who denies that Christ has come in the flesh, this one is antichrist” (1 John 4:2-3)
last_rejected.source_quote: Certe qui negat Christum in carne venisse, hic antichristus est.
last_rejected.why: English adds a citation to 1 John that is not present in the Latin source, misattributing the statement.
last_rejected.fix: “He who denies that Christ has come in the flesh is antichrist.”
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'qui negat Christum in carne venisse, hic antichristus est' is indeed 1 John 4:2-3; citation is correct, not misattributed.

last_rejected.quote: So let those blush who assert that the flesh sits in the heavens
last_rejected.source_quote: sine qua nec ipse esse poterit nec agnosci: ut et illi erubescant qui adfirmant
last_rejected.why: Purpose/result of the future recognition is turned into Tertullian’s exhortation, and “also” is dropped.
last_rejected.fix: without which he will be able neither to exist nor to be recognized, so that those too may blush who assert that the flesh sits in the heavens
last_rejected.ruling: "ut et illi erubescant" is a subjunctive purpose clause ("so that those too may blush"); "So let those blush" is a loose but acceptable rendering, and the dropped "et" is minor.
